program_name: International Management (MIM) - Master's Degree / Laurea Magistrale in International Management
teaching_language: Case (1): fully English-taught. The programme page records LANGUAGE: English, and the 2026/27 admission call states the selection is for admission to 'the Master's Degree in International Management (MIM) taught in English'; the binding Italian version reads 'corso di laurea magistrale interamente in lingua inglese in International Management (MIM)'. No Italian language requirement is set for admission, and no Italian-language track exists inside this degree course. All lessons are held in person in Trento.
campus: Trento. Department of Economics and Management, via Vigilio Inama 5, 38122 Trento (TN). The programme page lists LOCATION: 'Department of Economics and Management, via Vigilio Inama, 5 - 38122 Trento (TN)'; lessons take place only in person.
degree_class: LM-77 (LM77) - Scienze economico-aziendali / Business Economics Sciences. Confirmed on the UniTrento orientation catalogue entry for MIM ('Classe di laurea: LM77 - Scienze economico aziendali') and in the degree's didactic regulations and ministerial RAD sheet.
admission_type: Restricted access - 'numero programmato' (the programme page states ACCESS: Programmed). Admission is by a public selection based on qualifications ('per titoli') plus, if appropriate, an interview - not by a TOLC or any national/standardised entrance exam. Total intake for a.y. 2026/2027 is 40 places, of which 30 are reserved for non-European citizens and the remaining places (10, as stated on the official EU admission page) go to Europeans and equivalents; unassigned non-EU reserved places are released to Europeans and equivalents within the overall limit. Two application calls: the first is open to all candidates, the second only to Europeans and equivalents. A non-refundable EUR 30 application fee applies to each application, and admitted candidates pay a EUR 100 enrolment-confirmation fee.
academic_requirements: 1) QUALIFICATION: a Bachelor's Degree (at least 3 years) or a higher qualification awarded in Italy, or another international qualification recognised as equivalent. Final-year undergraduates may apply provided the Bachelor's degree is obtained by 30 June 2026 for non-Europeans; by 31 October 2026 for Europeans and equivalents, and also by 31 October 2026 for non-European undergraduates who will obtain the qualification from an Italian university and hold a valid Italian study permit. UniTrento may require additional documentation (statement of verification and/or statement of comparability) through the CIMEA DiploMe service. 2) CURRICULAR CREDITS: at least 60 university credits (CFU) certifying a good knowledge of economics, business administration, statistics, mathematical methods for economics and private law, specifically in the scientific-disciplinary sectors SECS-P/01 (ECON-01/A), SECS-P/02 (ECON-02/A), SECS-P/07 (ECON-06/A), SECS-P/08 (ECON-07/A), SECS-S/01 (STAT-01/A), SECS-S/06 (STAT-04/A) and IUS/01 (GIUR-01/A). For qualifications obtained abroad, the Selection Committee assesses whether the study plan meets these binding requirements. 3) SEATS: 40 places in total for a.y. 2026/2027, including a reserved quota of 30 places for non-European citizens; the official EU admission page states 'Seats available: 10 (limited number)' for Europeans and equivalents. Unassigned non-EU reserved seats are made available to Europeans and equivalents within the overall limit. 4) SELECTION SCORE: the Selection Committee awards up to 100 points - up to 40 points for the curriculum studiorum; up to 10 points for international certifications (English language proficiency and GMAT/GRE, if held); up to 50 points for statement of purpose, reference letters and the Committee's overall evaluation. Candidates scoring 50/100 or more are eligible; a candidate scoring less than 25 points in the statement-of-purpose/reference-letters/overall section is not admitted even if the total exceeds 50. 5) TRANSFERS: students already enrolled in another Master's degree or at another university may request a transfer only after passing the selection and receiving a positive evaluation by the Admission Committee; they must contact mim@unitn.it by 29 May 2026 for the preliminary credit assessment. Those not meeting the requirements for the second year are admitted to the first year. 6) Non-European admitted students must complete consular pre-enrolment on Universitaly and obtain their visa no later than 30 September 2026; all admitted students must be enrolled at UniTrento no later than 31 October 2026.
language_requirements: ENGLISH: minimum B2 of the CEFR is mandatory. It may be certified in any of the following ways: (a) an international certificate among those listed in the call - IELTS (overall min. 6), TOEFL (overall min. 72; IELTS Indicator and TOEFL Home Edition are accepted), Cambridge ESOL FCE / CAE / CPE / Bulats min. 60 / BEC Vantage / BEC Higher, City & Guilds ESOL Communicator + Spoken English Communicator, ESOL Expert + Spoken English Expert, ESOL Mastery + Spoken English Mastery, Trinity College London ISE II / ISE III / ISE IV, LCCI English for Business Level 2 / 3 / 4, Jetset level 5 / 6 / 7, Pearson General English Test Level 3 / 4 / 5, Pearson Academic English Test (min. score 42), or a GMAT test with a minimum score of 580 (the official admission web pages additionally specify 'GMAT score 580 or higher for GMAT Classic Edition' and 'GMAT score 545 or higher for GMAT Focus Edition'); unless otherwise specified by the awarding institution, certificates are valid for 5 years; (b) having passed a B2 (or higher) English language exam during previous university studies; (c) holding a Bachelor's or Master's degree run entirely in English (to be certified); (d) being an English mother-tongue speaker - a self-certification is required stating that the whole of primary and secondary education was completed in that language. The Admission Committee may call an interview in order to verify the applicant's English level. English proficiency also contributes to the score (up to 10 points together with GMAT/GRE). ITALIAN: no Italian language requirement for admission or enrolment; the programme is delivered entirely in English.
required_documents: Uploaded in the online application on the UniTrento Apply portal (access via SPID, CIE, an @unitn.it username, or a provisional @guest.unitn.it account that should be created at least 48 hours before the deadline): (1) copy of the passport (non-Europeans) or identity card (Europeans and equivalents not registering with a digital identity); (2) copy of the Bachelor's degree diploma, if already awarded - candidates with a degree issued by, or enrolled at, an Italian university may upload a self-declaration; (3) transcript of records listing exams, marks/results, credits and grade point average (if available), in Italian or English - self-declaration allowed for Italian university degrees/enrolment; (4) CV in English (PDF, no specific layout required); (5) proof of English proficiency at B2 as described in Art. 2 of the call; (6) GMAT or GRE score - not compulsory (the official admission pages state a minimum GMAT score accepted of 500 for this optional attachment); (7) statement of purpose - the applicant answers a few questions in English [uncertain] (on the official non-EU admission page these are: why do you want to study International Management; why with us; how could you contribute to the class / what is your added value; what do you want to achieve professionally); (8) at least two reference letters in English or Italian on letterhead, uploaded by the applicant within the deadline (letters sent by other means are not considered), plus the contacts of at least two referees entered in the application; (9) optionally, documentation of other relevant experiences or specialisations. An official translation is required for any document not issued in English or Italian; illegible documents are not considered and incomplete or unsubmitted applications are excluded. A non-refundable application fee of EUR 30.00 must be paid within the application deadline, otherwise the applicant is automatically excluded. Admitted candidates then pay a EUR 100 enrolment-confirmation fee (waived for second-call admitted candidates who complete enrolment within 7 days of the admission notice); admitted non-Europeans must additionally complete pre-enrolment on Universitaly (within 2 weeks of confirmation) at the Italian embassy/consulate and obtain a study visa.
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance exam and no TOLC/CISIA test. Admission is a 'public selection based on qualifications and (if appropriate) interview' assessed by a Selection Committee of at least three members, scoring up to 100 points (curriculum studiorum up to 40; international certifications - English proficiency and GMAT/GRE - up to 10; statement of purpose, reference letters and overall evaluation up to 50). An interview may be requested by the Committee if the submitted documents do not provide enough information, and the Committee may also call an interview to verify the candidate's English level. GMAT/GRE are optional (they add score points; a GMAT of at least 580 Classic Edition / 545 Focus Edition can alternatively serve as proof of English B2). Eligibility threshold: 50/100 overall, with a minimum of 25 points in the statement-of-purpose/reference-letters/overall-evaluation section. Rankings are published on the programme's admission web pages by 30 April 2026 (first call) and by 31 July 2026 (second call).
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027, two calls for Europeans and equivalents. First call: applications from 17 December 2025 to 4 March 2026 at 12:00 (noon) CET. Second call: applications from 15 April 2026 to 29 May 2026 at 12:00 (noon) CET (reserved for Europeans and equivalents only). Ranking published by 30 April 2026 (first call) and by 31 July 2026 (second call). Bachelor's degree to be obtained by 31 October 2026; enrolment at UniTrento by 31 October 2026. Application fee EUR 30 per application. Both 2026/2027 calls were closed at the time of research (31 August 2026).
application_deadline_non_eu: A.y. 2026/2027: first call only - applications from 17 December 2025 to 4 March 2026 at 12:00 (noon) CET. Non-Europeans may not apply in the second call. Ranking by 30 April 2026. Bachelor's degree to be obtained by 30 June 2026 (or by 31 October 2026 for non-European undergraduates graduating from an Italian university while holding a valid Italian study permit). After confirmation: pre-enrolment on Universitaly within 2 weeks, study visa to be obtained no later than 30 September 2026, and enrolment at UniTrento no later than 31 October 2026.
tuition_or_fees_link: Non-EU citizens: https://www.unitn.it/en/study/fees-scholarships-accommodation/tuition-fees/non-eu-citizens/masters-degrees-english (maximum EUR 6,500 per year; first-year amount set by admission score - tuition waiver for 90-100, EUR 1,000 for 70-89.9, EUR 3,000 for 60-69.9, EUR 6,500 for 50-59.9; second-year amount set by credits earned by 10 August 2027 - waiver for >=42 CFU, EUR 1,000 for 36-41, EUR 3,000 for 24-35, EUR 6,500 for 6-23, EUR 10,000 for <6). EU and equivalent citizens: https://www.unitn.it/en/study/fees-scholarships-accommodation/tuition-fees/eu-and-related-countries (income-based, calculated on the ISEE Universita indicator); general page https://www.unitn.it/en/study/fees-scholarships-accommodation/tuition-fees . Scholarships: UniTrento awards scholarships (with full tuition waiver) to top-scoring non-European applicants with a score of at least 70/100 - the number is announced with the ranking, no separate application is needed, and the scholarship is not compatible with other Italian public scholarships (MAECI, Unicolor, Invest your Talent in Italy). Separate mandatory costs: EUR 30 application fee, EUR 100 enrolment-confirmation fee.

uncertainty_notes: 1) SOURCE ACCESS / WAF: at the time of research (31 August 2026) corsi.unitn.it returned HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed to direct requests (Cloudflare/WAF bot protection). All corsi.unitn.it content above - programme page, both admission pages, and the full 12-page English and Italian 2026/27 admission calls - was read from Internet Archive captures of the official URLs: programme page captured 14 August 2026, admission pages captured 16 February 2026, English call PDF and Italian binding call PDF captured 10 March 2026. orienta.unitn.it, www.unitn.it and webapps.unitn.it were reachable directly. Figures should be re-verified against the live pages once corsi.unitn.it is reachable again. 2) SEAT ARITHMETIC: the call states 40 total places including 30 reserved for non-Europeans, without printing the EU figure; the official EU admission page states 'Seats available: 10', which is consistent (40 - 30 = 10). Unassigned non-EU reserved places roll over to Europeans and equivalents within the overall limit, so the effective EU number can be higher than 10. 3) COPY-PASTE ERROR ON THE OFFICIAL EU PAGE: the 'Documents to upload' section of the Europeans-and-equivalents admission page lists statement-of-purpose questions belonging to a different programme ('Why do you want to study Behavioural and Applied Economics?' / 'What do you want to achieve professionally by studying within the Master of Behavioural and Applied Economics?'). The non-Europeans page carries the correct International Management questions, which are the ones reported in required_documents. Applicants should follow the questions actually shown in the online application form. 4) GMAT THRESHOLD INCONSISTENCY: the admission call names GMAT 580 only as one way of proving English B2, whereas both official admission web pages add a GMAT Focus Edition equivalent of 545 (not present in the call PDF) and separately state 'minimum GMAT score accepted: 500' for the optional GMAT/GRE attachment that contributes to the score. These are two different uses of the GMAT (English proof vs. scoring) and the 545 Focus figure has no counterpart in the binding Italian call. 5) BINDING VERSION: the English call is an explicit courtesy translation - 'The only binding version is the Italian one'. All key figures (40/30 places, 4 March and 29 May 2026 deadlines, 50/100 eligibility, 30 April and 31 July 2026 rankings, fee brackets) were cross-checked against the Italian binding PDF and match. 6) ADMISSION YEAR: 2026/2027 is the most recent published year; both of its calls had already closed at the time of research and the UniTrento Apply portal showed 'No active applications for this type'. The 2027/2028 call had not yet been published (the 2026/27 first call opened on 17 December 2025, so the next one is expected around December 2026). 7) SPECIAL AGREEMENTS / DOUBLE DEGREES: Art. 3.3 of the call notes that 'Applicants who are going to take part in the selection within special Agreements, may apply to the Master according to different deadlines and procedures settled in the Agreements'. The orientation page mentions dual-degree partnerships with universities in the Netherlands and Germany and a mandatory internship, usually abroad; the specific partner universities and their separate deadlines were not verified from an accessible official source. 8) INTERVIEW: an interview is possible but not systematic - it is called only 'if appropriate', when the submitted documents are insufficient, or to verify the candidate's English level. 9) NO ENTRANCE TEST: unlike the Department's bachelor programmes, MIM uses no TOLC/CISIA or other standardised entrance test; GMAT/GRE are optional score-enhancing attachments.
